source_signature.notes: Batch 4J skill 5/5, BATCH CLOSER. Owns identification of zero-force members BY INSPECTION, without computing the full set of member forces, and owns the two standard rules together with the CONDITIONS each requires. Rule 1: a joint connecting exactly two non-collinear members and carrying no applied load and no support reaction makes both members zero-force. Rule 2: a joint connecting exactly three members of which two are collinear, carrying no applied load and no support reaction, makes the third member zero-force. Owns the discipline of checking every condition before applying a rule - member count, collinearity, and absence of any load or reaction. Boundary: method_of_joints (signed, skill 2) computes member forces by joint equilibrium and explicitly cedes inspection identification here; the artifact carries the complement - this skill identifies by rule without solving the truss and does not compute the remaining member forces. method_of_sections excluded. member_tension_compression_signs (signed, skill 4) states that a zero-force member has no sign to assign; the complement is stated here - a zero-force member is neither in tension nor in compression. simple_truss_modeling (signed) supplies the idealisation the rules depend on and the artifact states plainly that the rules are invalid without it. truss_support_reactions (signed, skill 1) - a joint carrying a support reaction counts as LOADED for these rules, so reaction PRESENCE must be checked even though reaction VALUES are never computed. Worked example Operator-verified independently: joints A(0,0) pin, B(4,0), C(8,0), D(12,0) roller on the bottom chord and E(4,3), F(8,3) on the top; nine members AB, BC, CD, AE, EF, FD, BE, BF, CF, with m = 2j - 3 = 9, determinate; single applied load 12 kN downward at E. Inspection joint by joint: joint A has two members and no applied load BUT a pin reaction acts there, so Rule 1 does not apply; joint B has the collinear bottom-chord pair BA and BC and no load, which resembles Rule 2, BUT four members meet there rather than exactly three, so Rule 2 does not apply; joint C has exactly three members with CB and CD collinear and neither load nor reaction, so every condition of Rule 2 is met and CF is ZERO-FORCE; joint D has two members and no applied load BUT a roller reaction acts there, so Rule 1 does not apply; joints E and F satisfy no rule. Result by inspection: CF only. Distinguishing feature bites: the result is reachable by inspection alone, and THREE distinct near-miss joints fail on TWO different conditions - support reaction present at A and at D, member count at B - so a student cannot pattern-match on shape and must check conditions. VERIFICATION PRECEDES REPORT in both arrays and confirms rather than produces the result: at joint C the unit directions are (-1,0) toward B, (+1,0) toward D and (0,+1) toward F, so summing vertical components leaves only CF and gives F_CF = 0. The conclusion uses no reaction value and no other member force, which is precisely what makes it an inspection result. HONEST LIMITATION recorded in concept, procedure, solution and common_errors: a zero-force member is zero FOR THIS LOADING ONLY. It is not redundant and must not be removed - under a different load case it may carry force, and such members commonly brace long members or serve other cases. A student who concludes from a correct answer that CF could be deleted has learned the wrong thing. TWO-signal mapping: axis_confusion at step 3 (the collinearity determination - treating two non-collinear members as collinear, or failing to recognise a collinear chord pair, when comparing unit directions at a joint; its trigger opens by stipulating that member counts and load/reaction presence have already been recorded, which partitions it from step 4), unclassified at step 4 (applying a rule without every condition met). sign_or_placement_error OMITTED: a zero-force member carries no sign, so nothing earns it. solution_sequencing_error OMITTED: the joints may be inspected in any order and no authored step strands a prerequisite unknown. simple_average_used omitted (Centroids-family). Trig-resolution cross-check N/A recorded affirmatively: no inclined vector is decomposed from a stated angle. No archetype is asserted while PROCEDURE-ARCHETYPE-LIBRARY-V1 remains unapproved. SIGNAL-VOCABULARY GAP RECORDED AND ROUTED TO THE ARCHITECT, not force-fit and with no new signal proposed: the unclassified mapping at step 4 carries SEVEN distinct error classes - ignoring a support reaction at a two-member joint, applying Rule 2 at a four-member joint, miscounting members at a joint, treating an identified zero-force member as permanently redundant, skipping the verification, computing remaining member forces or reaction values, and assigning a tension or compression designation to a zero-force member. A student who errs cannot be routed to a remedy, because the diagnostic can say only that something in the boundary went wrong. This is the THIRD independent instance of the gap for identification, modelling and classification skills, after the Wave 1 records on simple_truss_modeling, constraints_static_determinacy and dry_friction_static_kinetic, and it is the most severe ratio observed. Two further Operator observations recorded, neither corrected: first, the axis_confusion earn at step 3 is the corpus's most marginal - procedure step 3 genuinely authors a directional comparison so the mapping meets the stated criterion, but collinearity RECOGNITION is a weaker relative of the component-ASSIGNMENT errors that earned this signal elsewhere, and the worked example does not exercise it because every collinear pair in it is exactly horizontal; second, the term near-miss appears in solution_steps and in the answer, which is authoring vocabulary rather than domain vocabulary, though it describes a real property of those joints rather than the diagnostic apparatus and so reads as instructional. Review beat cleared at first pass; no correction lane. CLOSES BATCH 4J 5/5.
